tasks.short: Sort items and return them to shelves

steps.what: Sort books and publications according to the established procedure
Return items to shelves, files, or designated storage areas
Show the other storage area named in the procedure

tasks.design: The assistant sorts books and publications by the written procedure and carries them back to the shelf, file, or other storage area. {DOCS} shows the storage area when the item identifier is already stored. A missing area stays blank, and the assistant chooses the spot.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shelf mark lived on the item, and the assistant walked the whole round without a stored area.
tasks.enabler_now: The area is a field on the item record, so a known identifier can be shown.
tasks.still_hard: Sorting the pile and walking it back to the shelf stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant sees a damaged item or a broken sequence and places it by the procedure, not by the screen.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the shelving round. The assistant can see a stored area before the walk.

reach.task: Set the shelf procedure for a collection
reach.learn: Which area the procedure names when the record is blank.

evidence.claim: A stored item identifier can show a storage area. Sorting and reshelving stay manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a returned pile and ends when each item is in a shelf, file, or storage area.
A location row has item identifier and storage area, entered by the assistant when the item was processed. A missing area is left blank.
No send or record write is added. The one-hour upkeep corrects a blank area the assistant has just confirmed.
unknowns: How often the stored area is blank or wrong.
research_questions: Which piles were shelved from the stored area, and which the assistant placed by the procedure?

already_counted.description: Returning items to shelves, files, or storage areas is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a storage area after the assistant confirms the right spot.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most items have no stored area, so the walk is unchanged. High: known items show an area, and sorting plus the walk remain. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Open and close the library and secure equipment

steps.what: Read the specified hours from the library notice
Open the library during the specified hours
Close the library and secure computers and audio-visual equipment

tasks.design: The assistant opens and closes the library and locks computers and audio-visual equipment. {DOCS} shows the specified hours for that site. A missing hours row stays blank, and the assistant follows the posted notice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hours were a paper notice, and securing equipment was a memory list.
tasks.enabler_now: The hours are a stored row the assistant can open at the door.
tasks.still_hard: Unlocking, the walk-round, and locking equipment stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant sees an unlocked room or a missing cable and does not leave it.
tasks.altitude: Nothing material changes in the week. The hours are visible at the door.

reach.learn: Which hours apply when the library notice is blank.

evidence.claim: A stored site row can show opening hours. Opening, closing, and locking equipment stay manual.

assumptions: The work starts at the door and ends when the library is open or the equipment is secured.
An hours row has site identifier, open time, and close time, entered by the facilities colleague. A missing row is left blank.
Existing door alarms are not counted as the assistant's time. Upkeep is zero because no new list is kept.
unknowns: Who is allowed to hold the equipment keys.
research_questions: On which days was the hours row blank, so the assistant used the posted notice?

already_counted.description: Closing the library and securing equipment is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: No new upkeep: opening, closing, and locking do not add a record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the hours row is often blank, so the round is unchanged. High: the hours are on the row, and locking equipment still takes the round. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read locations, including books, periodicals, and pictures
Locate Braille volumes, tape cassettes, and other library materials for patrons

tasks.design: The assistant locates books, periodicals, pictures, Braille volumes, and tape cassettes for patrons. {DOCS} returns the location when the title identifier is stored. A missing location stays blank, and the assistant searches the shelf.
tasks.previous_blocker: The call number was read from a card, then the assistant walked the stack.
tasks.enabler_now: A known title identifier can return a location without a second card search.
tasks.still_hard: Walking the stack, and finding an item that was not checked in, stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices a misshelved item and tells the patron when it is not there.
tasks.altitude: The assistant still walks the stack. A known title shows its location first.

reach.task: Answer a location the catalogue does not hold
reach.learn: Which collections are kept off the main location list.

evidence.claim: A stored title identifier can return a location. Fetching the item for the patron stays manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a patron request and ends when the item is in hand or the assistant says it is not found.
A holding row has title identifier, format, and location, entered when the item was processed. A missing location is left blank.
The hour of upkeep corrects a location after the assistant finds the item elsewhere.
unknowns: How often a requested title has no location row.
research_questions: Which requests were found from the location, and which needed a stack search?

already_counted.description: Locating materials on the shelf for patrons is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a location after the assistant finds the item on a different shelf.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many requests have no location, so the stack search remains. High: known titles show a location, and the walk to fetch them remains. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Enter the patrons' fields on the computers
Assemble the draft patrons' record from those fields
Review the draft patrons' record before the update
Update the patrons' records on the computers

tasks.design: The assistant enters the patron fields on the computer. {DOCS} assembles a draft record and writes it only after the assistant accepts that version. A missing name, address, or card number stays blank and the update does not run.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant retyped the whole record into the computer, including fields that had not changed.
tasks.enabler_now: The fields are a form, so an unchanged field can be copied and a blank required field can stop the write.
tasks.still_hard: The assistant still types a new address and still checks the person in front of them.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant refuses a record that does not match the identification the patron showed.

ambition.what: A complete patron record is updated the same day, and an incomplete one waits.

tasks.altitude: The assistant still takes the details. The accepted version is what gets stored.

reach.task: Decide a registration the desk cannot complete
reach.learn: Which fields the library requires before a card is valid.

evidence.claim: A form can assemble a patron record from entered fields and stop when a required field is blank.
A patron record is personal data. The assistant accepts the version before it is stored. The design does not score patrons. National rules on staff consultation differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a patron detail changes and ends when the accepted record is stored or the assistant stops.
The assistant enters patron identifier, name, address, and card number. A blank required field is not invented.
The write uses the version accepted in the review step. A later edit voids that acceptance.
unknowns: Which address fields the library treats as required.
research_questions: How many updates stopped on a blank field, and how many the assistant accepted?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the draft patron record is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a patron field when the assistant finds the accepted version was wrong.

approvals.approved_version: patron record version the assistant accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: patrons still dictate every field, so the assistant types as today. High: only changed fields are typed, and the assistant still accepts the version. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant still meets patrons, shelves items, and handles cash. A record, notice, invoice, or order is written or sent only after the assistant accepts that version.
reach: A librarian receives the question the assistant could not answer from the desk.
A finance colleague receives only an invoice the assistant has accepted.
skills_to_grow: Stop when a required field is blank.
Accept or refuse the exact version before a send or a write.
Keep shelving, cash, and patron conversations in their own hands.
role.ambitious_version: Every item on loan has a location and a due date the desk can trust, and the assistant still decides the exception.
